sections.h2: Which Davidson County offices bill and value property?
sections.html:
Davidson County runs its property tax through a Tax Assessor side that lists and values property and a Tax Collector side that bills and collects. Both are found at 913 Greensboro Street, 3rd Floor, Suite 303, in Lexington (NC 27292), open weekdays from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. A second counter in Denton opens at 8:30 AM on weekdays.

  • Tax office and appeals line: 336-242-2160.
  • Collections line: 336-242-2180.
  • Mailing address for the assessor: P.O. Box 1617, Lexington, NC 27293.
  • Mailing address for payments: Davidson County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 1577, Lexington, NC 27293.

The county's Collections page says questions about listing, billing and assessed values go to the assessor's side, while the collector is responsible only for collecting what is owed.

sections.h2: What are the 2026 Davidson County tax rates?
sections.html:
The county's own line reads 0.5400 on the 2026 sheet, and a parcel inside a city, school district or fire district picks up that jurisdiction's line too. The sheet carries the word tentative in its heading, so verify the adopted numbers with the tax office.

City motor vehicle fees are $30.00 in Lexington and High Point, $20.00 in Thomasville and $5.00 in Denton, and the Lexington sheet notes that discounts are not applied to the city and municipal service district lines.

sections.h2: When are Davidson County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Bills for land, buildings and business or personal items are mailed each July. They fall due September 1 and carry no interest until after January 5. A weekend January 5 pushes the deadline to the following business day.

The county gives a 1 1/2 percent discount for payment in July and a 1 percent discount in August. A January 5 postmark counts as timely, though the county advises mailing a full week early. Past-due real estate accounts are charged 2 percent for January and an extra 3/4 percent each month after that, which matches the state schedule. Payment plans have to be arranged when the annual bill arrives and finished by the delinquent date, and card payments are taken at the office.

sections.h2: What is happening with the Davidson County revaluation?
sections.html:
Davidson County's last revaluation took effect January 1, 2021, and the county's pages say the planned 2026 revaluation was postponed until 2027 under new legislation. State law requires counties to reappraise at least once every eight years, and the county reviews more than 97,000 parcels in a revaluation.

The county explains that revaluation is meant to equalize values, not raise revenue, and that tax rates are set by elected officials in June. Owners who appealed their 2026 or 2027 values on time do not need to refile, and any change from those appeals will apply to the 2027 tax year. The informal appeal deadline for the 2026 round was 5:00 PM on Thursday, April 30, 2026, and it has passed. The county's appeal page offers separate forms for the current 2026 value and the 2027 revaluation value, and the revaluation help address is revalhelp@davidsoncountync.gov.

sections.h2: What steps does a Davidson County owner follow to contest a value?
sections.html:
Appeals have three levels, and the first is an informal review with a county appraiser, who looks at your property record and any supporting evidence with you. If an error turns up, it can be fixed without a formal appeal.

The second step is a formal hearing at the county's Board of Equalization and Review. Under state law the commissioners sit as that board unless a special one is created; Davidson County describes its board as local residents with real estate knowledge, appointed by the commissioners. A written notice to the state Property Tax Commission is the step after an unwelcome board decision. The county lists reasons that do not count as grounds:

  • The size of the percentage increase or decrease.
  • A market value above the insurance value.
  • A feeling that the value is simply too high.
  • An owner's inability to pay the tax.

sections.h2: Which property tax relief programs can a Davidson County owner use?
sections.html:
State law sets up three homestead programs and lets each owner use just one. The first program, for older or disabled owners, excludes whichever is bigger: $25,000 or half the appraised value. Qualifying means being 65 or older, or disabled for good, and earning no more than $38,800 for 2026.

The circuit breaker is the second: it holds the bill to 4.0 percent of income for owners at or below the limit, and to 5.0 percent for owners whose income reaches 150 percent of it ($58,200 for 2026). Five years of owning and occupying the home come first. The third takes $45,000 off the value for a disabled veteran with no age or income test. Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor, and the county's property information page links to the homestead application. Any tax deferred under the circuit breaker turns into a lien and becomes payable when the property transfers, which matters at a sale.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Davidson County property tax?
sections.html:
Interest starts on a bill after the January 5 deadline, and after that the bill is subject to collection actions. The collector lists wage garnishment, attachment of bank accounts or rents, levy on personal property and, for real estate, tax foreclosure by sale at public auction.

  • Unpaid real estate accounts can be advertised in local newspapers from March 1 to June 30, at added cost to the taxpayer.
  • The county also lists sheriff's warrants, in rem foreclosures and attachment of the state tax refund.
  • State law sets the lien date as the listing date, so the lien exists before the bill is due.

The county posts a PDF list of 2025 delinquent taxpayers and a tax foreclosure list. If a sale is pending, Davidson County also requires a tax certificate before the Register of Deeds takes a deed, so a delinquent balance has to be cleared first.

sections.h2: What does the Census count in Davidson County?
sections.html:
The Census estimate for July 2025 is 180,182 residents, and the five-year survey counts 69,846 households, 74.4 percent of them owning. The median owned home is valued at $219,100. Monthly costs for owners carrying a mortgage come to $1,355 at the median, and the median household brings in $64,172 (2024 dollars).

The county's rate sheet lists Lexington, Thomasville, Denton, Wallburg, Midway and High Point as taxing cities and towns, along with two school districts and dozens of fire districts. Ask the tax office which of those lines apply to your parcel.

sections.h2: How should I handle taxes when I sell a Davidson County house?
sections.html:
Ask whether the seller's share of the current bill is prorated at closing, and if you want zero exposure, have the closing attorney pay the collector from the proceeds. Per the county, selling during the year does not release the January 1 owner from that year's bill.

Request a tax certificate early if no attorney is closing. Check the 2026 or 2027 appeal status too, because a value change from an appeal lands in the 2027 tax year.

faqs.q: When are Davidson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment is due September 1, with no interest through January 5. July payments earn a 1 1/2 percent discount and August payments earn 1 percent.

faqs.q: What is the Davidson County tax rate?
faqs.a: County-only is 0.5400 on the 2026 sheet, and cities, schools and fire districts add their own rates. Lexington is printed at 0.6500 and Thomasville at 0.6200, and the sheet is marked tentative, so confirm final rates with the tax office.

faqs.q: Was the Davidson County revaluation postponed?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says its 2026 revaluation was postponed until 2027 under new legislation. Appeals filed on time for 2026 or 2027 values still get reviewed, and any change applies to the 2027 tax year.

faqs.q: How can I contest my Davidson County property value?
faqs.a: Start by filing the county's form for an informal sit-down with an appraiser. Only if that falls short does the matter go on to a formal hearing. The state Property Tax Commission hears later appeals, and the 30 days run from the board's mailing date.

faqs.q: What interest applies to late Davidson County taxes?
faqs.a: Past-due real estate accounts are charged 2 percent for January and 3/4 percent for each month after that. The county urges mailing payments at least five business days before the January 5 deadline.
